130605-N-AX577-138

U'TAPAO AIR BASE, Thailand (June 5, 2013) -  A Sailor from Naval Mobile Construction Battalion 5 smoothes stucco on the roof of a new structure built using the Saebi Alternative Building System, a concrete construction method that incorporates enhanced concrete spread over Styrofoam core, during a bi-lateral construction project with the Royal Thai Marines within Cooperation Afloat Readiness and Training (CARAT) exercise Thailand 2013.  U.S. Navy ships participating in the exercise include the dry cargo and ammunition ship USNS Washington Chambers (T-AKE 11), the amphibious dock landing ship USS Tortuga (LSD 46) with embarked U.S. Marine Corps landing force, diving and salvage vessel USNS Safeguard (T-ARS 50) with embarked Mobile Diving and Salvage Unit (MDSU) 1, and the guided missile destroyer USS Curtis Wilbur (DDG 54).  CARAT is a series of bilateral military exercises between the U.S. Navy and the armed forces of Bangladesh, Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Timor Leste.  (U.S. Navy photo by Mass Communication Specialist 1st Class Patrick Dille) (RELEASED)

images.caption: U.S. Marines with the 3rd Reconnaissance Battalion, 3rd Marine Division, III Marine Expeditionary Force jump out the back of a KC-130J Hercules aircraft while conducting aerial delivery training during exercise Cobra Gold 2013 near U-Tapao Royal Thai Navy Airfield in Rayong province, Thailand, Feb. 15, 2013. The U.S. Marines participated in the training with Royal Thai Marines. Cobra Gold is a regularly scheduled joint/combined exercise designed to ensure regional peace and strengthen the ability of the Royal Thai Armed Forces to defend Thailand or respond to regional contingencies. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Lance Cpl. Todd Michalek/Released)
